title: The 11 Best Food Processors Under $100
metaDescription: Our 11 picks for food processors under $100, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at food processors under $100 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 70725A 12-Cup Stack and Snap Food Processor
products.blurb: Key specs: 12-cup work bowl with 450-watt motor, Stack and Snap assembly, blade locks into the lid for one-handed setup, Includes slicing disc and shredding disc.
strengths: Adequate power for chopping, dips, and shredding 1 to 3 times per week without strain
Wide brand support and easy parts replacement through Hamilton Beach
limitations: 450W motor requires 1 to 2 minute cooling breaks on sustained 3+ minute runs
Blade dulls faster than premium Cuisinart stainless over 12 to 18 months
No variable speed, pulse and continuous only
Bowl seal can develop slight play over time, occasionally leaking on liquid-heavy recipes
features: 12-cup work bowl with 450-watt motor
Stack and Snap assembly, blade locks into the lid for one-handed setup
Includes slicing disc and shredding disc
Bowl-and-blade stacking system for compact storage
Dishwasher-safe bowl, lid, blade, and discs

strengths: 1,000W motor is the most powerful in this price tier by a wide margin
Handles dough and harder vegetables noticeably better than any Hamilton Beach at the same price
Auto-iQ presets remove guesswork on chop and puree consistency
limitations: Louder at full speed than mid-power competitors in this roundup
Auto-iQ programs limit manual pulse control for cooks who prefer to judge texture themselves
Taller housing than Hamilton Beach models, less ideal for tight cabinet clearance
